newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reform would give lift to German tax income-paper.
newsitem.headline: Reform would give lift to German tax income-paper.

text.p: Germany stands to lose billions of marks in tax revenues over the next few years, if it does not pass a tax reform package, the newsweekly Focus reported on Saturday.

Tax reform could lift the economy and bring federal, state and local governments 135 billion marks in additional tax income through the year 2001, the Institute for the German Economy (IDW) said in a report commissioned by the magazine.
If the government's tax plan had been in place this year, tax revenues would have been 8.1 billion marks higher, IDW estimated.
IDW said the tax package would have boosted economic growth by a nominal one percent, compared to the government's expectation of a real 0.5 percent rise in economic output.
Bonn's plan to cut 30 billion marks in taxes was blocked by opposition Social Democrats in parliamentary mediation last week.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition has sought the reforms to boost the economy and ease a gaping budget deficit.
